extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and researchers assessing non-systematic (narrative) review manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: A 6-item instrument (SANRA) for editors/reviewers to rate the methodological and reporting quality of non-systematic (narrative) review articles; each item is scored 0 (low) to 2 (high) and items are summed to form an overall quality score. The scale is intended to complement journal-specific evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of the review’s importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the manuscript justifies the importance of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item scored 0 (low standard) to 2 (high standard). The authors developed recommendations and examples to guide users filling out the instrument. In testing, raters often disagreed on this item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aims of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of clarity and appropriateness of the review’s aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item scored 0 (low standard) to 2 (high standard). Recommendations and examples accompany the item to guide ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature search description
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the manuscript describes the literature search (how sources were identified/selected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item scored 0 (low standard) to 2 (high standard). Recommendations and examples provided. In testing this item had the lowest corrected item–total correlation (0.33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether referencing is adequate — appropriate, sufficient, and correctly used to support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item scored 0 (low standard) to 2 (high standard). Recommendations and examples provided. Raters often disagreed on this item in the field test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of levels of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the manuscript presents levels of evidence (e.g., distinguishes between types/strengths of evidence) relevant to its arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item scored 0 (low standard) to 2 (high standard). Accompanying recommendations and examples help raters judge whether levels of evidence are adequately presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of data central to the article’s argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how well the manuscript presents data that are central to its argument (clarity, relevance, and sufficiency of data presentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item scored 0 (low standard) to 2 (high standard). Recommendations and examples provided. In testing this item showed the highest corrected item–total correlation (0.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item scoring convention (0–2 per item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the six SANRA items is rated on a three-point scale: 0 = low standard, 1 = moderate/acceptable, 2 = high standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should apply the provided recommendations and examples to choose the appropriate score for each item. The scale is designed for quick use (≈5 minutes) in editorial work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total score and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Total SANRA score is the sum of the six item scores (possible range 0–12) and is used to summarize overall reporting/quality of non-systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the field test of 30 manuscripts the mean (SD) sum score was 6.0 (2.6), observed range 1–12. The scale is intended to complement — not replace — journal-specific manuscript evaluation (e.g., audience, originality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration, feasibility, and rater training
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical guidance about completing the scale and rater preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raters confirmed completing the scale takes approximately 5 minutes and the revised version is easier to understand than earlier versions. The authors recommend further rater training based on the recommendations and examples provided with the scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychometric properties and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported reliability and item statistics from the authors' field test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected item–total correlations ranged from 0.33 to 0.58. Cronbach's alpha for the six-item scale was 0.68. Intraclass correlation coefficient (average measure) was 0.77 (95% CI, 0.57–0.88). The authors note some rater disagreement on items 1 and 4 and removed a prior item addressing writing and accessibility because ratings differed considerably.
